## Further multi-annotator datasets (larger K: VADER sentiment, K = 9; ConvAbuse severity, K = 5)

Same protocol as the core benchmark (frozen mpnet features, 12 methods, 5 seeds, checkpoints selected offline on validation). ConvAbuse has only 2-7 annotators per exchange, so with m = 3 most items have no held-out rater (the held-out metrics rest on the items with more); m = 2 is added for it.

## Personalisation on SCUT: per-rater offsets (45 known raters, 15 held-out raters)

Per-rating NLL on test faces. `known` = the raters used for training, `new` = raters never seen (their offset is zero). alpha is the weight of the population consensus (the uniform distribution over the set of 3 known raters' ratings) in the training target, 1 - alpha that of the rater's own rating; hard-label losses use the own rating only. ratings = training faces per rater.

## Random-effects summary across problems, soft-CORN minus baseline

d_i ~ N(mu, tau^2 + v_i) with v_i the corrected variance of problem i's seed differences; mu < 0 favours soft-CORN; tau is the between-problem standard deviation of the true difference. The probabilities are from the normal posterior of mu under a flat prior (ROPE as in the main tables). A stand-in for the Stan-based hierarchical test of Corani et al. (2017), which needs PyStan.
